line00
You just crossed thirty thousand dollars in sales. Did you just become a tax collector?
line01
For G-S-T, thirty thousand isn't per year. It's any four calendar quarters in a row.
line02
Say you billed five thousand, then eight, then nine, then nine and a half.
line03
That's thirty-one thousand, five hundred. Over the line.
line04
You stop being a small supplier at the end of the next month. Then you have twenty-nine days to register.
line05
Cross thirty thousand in a single quarter? You charge G-S-T on the very sale that put you over.
line06
After that, a thousand-dollar invoice in Manitoba carries fifty dollars of G-S-T.
line07
That fifty was never yours. You collect it for the government.
line08
The upside: G-S-T you pay on business costs comes back as input tax credits.
line09
In H-S-T provinces it's thirteen to fifteen percent. And provincial sales taxes have their own rules.
line10
Watch your last four quarters, not your tax year.
